transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's project huddle. As you know, the school has approved the concept of building a twelve-bed teaching garden beside the science wing, and I have final authority to approve the garden's construction, purchasing, and safety plan. The current draft plan calls for in-ground beds, a volunteer workday on October 18, a $3,000 charge to general funds, and standard latex gardening gloves. Before I can sign off on this campus project plan, I need each of you to report on the requirements you've verified. Let's start -- science teacher, please go first with any site or curricular requirements you've confirmed, followed by facilities coordinator, business manager, and school nurse.

transcript.text: I need to share an important site requirement before we proceed. I just received the soil test results yesterday from the proposed garden area, and the lead measurement came back at 180 parts per million. According to the district garden standard, at that reading we are required to remove the top six inches of soil and use raised beds instead of in-ground beds. This result came in after the draft plan was circulated, so I haven't entered it in the project folder yet, but it clearly affects our current plan's use of in-ground beds.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a facilities requirement that affects our timeline. My utility-locate request just came back this morning, and it cleared the site for work on October 28 -- not before that date. Facilities policy requires a posted site permit before any excavation or bed assembly can begin. Since the locate response only arrived this morning, it came after the draft workday of October 18 was proposed. This means we cannot proceed with excavation or bed assembly on October 18; the earliest date we can legally begin that work is October 28, once the site permit is posted.

However, the grant only applies to purchases covered by a purchase order issued before ordering, so we need to make sure a purchase order is in place before any purchases are made. The grant office sent me the award confirmation yesterday, and I haven't yet attached it to the draft budget.

transcript.text: I need to report a student-safety requirement that affects our purchasing and safety plan. My student health review, which I completed this week after the draft equipment list was prepared, identified a documented severe latex allergy among the students scheduled for garden instruction. Under our school safety protocol, this requires us to substitute nitrile-only gloves for the standard latex gardening gloves currently listed in the draft plan, and to post an allergy-safety notice at the garden entrance.
